tools.name: get_server_info
tools.description: Everything you need before your first call: where to send ADA, and how much. No API key required -- call this first, before 'register'.

tools.name: register
tools.description: Register a new API key by paying a one-time fee. Pay the registration fee (see get_server_info) from the Cardano address you want your key bound to, sending it to the operator's payment_address, then call this with that transaction's hash. The payment must already be CONFIRMED on-chain (wait ~20-30s

tools.name: check_payment_status
tools.description: Check whether a payment transaction is confirmed on-chain yet. Poll this after paying and before calling 'register', 'mint', or trusting a payment_tx you're about to reference -- submitting a transaction does not mean it is confirmed.

tools.name: prepare_payment
tools.description: Build an unsigned transaction that pays the mint fee from from_address to the operator, with change returned to from_address. tools.name: mint
tools.description: Mint an NFT after separately paying the mint fee (see prepare_payment or pay any other way, then wait for on-chain confirmation -- check_payment_status). tools.name: prepare_atomic_mint
tools.description: Build a single transaction that pays the mint fee from from_address AND mints the NFT to destination_address at the same time -- no separate payment step, no payment_tx. findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "check_payment_status" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Check whether a payment transaction is confirmed on-chain yet. Poll this after paying and before calling 'register', 'mint', or trusting a payment_tx you're abo…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "prepare_payment" references sensitive artifacts (private key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
